_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Portable final-pass quality enforcement across code, templates, skills, prompts, scripts, documentation, pages, and…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "reviewing a pull request for correctness, security, and style"
cases.context: The agent has access to the best-practice skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is best-practice the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes best-practice as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against skill-scaffold, color-system-design, typography-system
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the best-practice workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore best-practice
Does not route to skill-scaffold, color-system-design, typography-system when the best-practice scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence

cases.scenario: A user asks: "reviewing PR feedback phrasing and comment classification (use code-review)"
cases.context: This is a boundary test. The skill should avoid false-positive activation and route to the better owner when appropriate.
cases.question: Should best-practice be applied here? If not, what should happen instead?
expected_flags: Recognizes the request is outside best-practice's ownership
Routes the work to skill-scaffold or asks for the missing owner instead of forcing this skill
Preserves any real issue in the request without applying best-practice terminology incorrectly
expected_fix_hints: Decline to apply best-practice as the primary skill
Name the better owner or the boundary reason
Offer only a narrow handoff if best-practice has a secondary support role
absent_signals: Does not claim best-practice should own the request
Does not use best-practice's framework to solve an explicitly excluded problem
Does not suppress the correct adjacent owner
